checkOutcomes.evidence: The platform probe found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule, and default and dark-emulated screenshots are byte-identical (229,260 bytes).
Under emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, matchMedia was true and the page exposed no active animations or transition elements.
The forced-colors capture retained visible text, controls, current navigation state, and content boundaries.
CSS/DOM inspection found no view-transition-name, @view-transition, or startViewTransition usage across the listing and detail templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative templates contain no parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked animation to implement. No scroll handlers or animation timelines were observed.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked motion exists on the audited templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile navigation uses native horizontal overflow and content uses normal document scrolling; no custom pointer handlers fight platform gestures.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The templates have no sticky or affixed chrome whose state needs to react to scrolling.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip, popover, or floating menu was present in the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No anchored overlay exists on these templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Current navigation is visually highlighted, detail pages name the selected item above the player, and search results repeat the query as the section heading.
Initial and 12-second delayed screenshots show no interstitial, modal, or banner obscuring core content.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No visible transient overlay or disclosure control was present during representative loads.
checkOutcomes.reason: No overlay/disclosure primitive is used in the observed UI.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The listing and detail templates reserve most post-header space for thumbnails or the player, with compact navigation and controls.
At 360×800 the layout primitive reported scrollWidth=clientWidth=360, zero horizontal overflow, and a valid viewport meta tag.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Cards appear in one grid context per viewport and are not reused simultaneously in differently sized containers; viewport adaptation is already evidenced separately.
checkOutcomes.reason: No component is reused across independently sized containers on the audited templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The focused search field computed to outline: none and no box-shadow. The submit control measured 32×28 px and the text input 170×28 px, below the 44×44 CSS-pixel target guidance.
The homepage immediately identifies a new-video listing; cards are direct links, search is visible, and detail pages place the player directly beneath the title.
After 5 seconds on the detail page at desktop and mobile sizes, the 16:9 player showed a broken-document icon. The iframe URL was present, but the core playback surface did not render.
The detail screenshot shows only the browser broken-resource icon; there is no status text, retry action, or accessible error announcement near the player.
Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.0 s (score 0.77), above the 2.5 s good threshold, although the local trace measured 1.11 s and TBT remained low.
The mobile layout observer recorded CLS 0 with no shifts over five seconds; thumbnail dimensions reserve grid space.
The trace and layout observers found zero long tasks and total blocking time of 0–10.5 ms.
Lighthouse identified a Google font stylesheet with about 812 ms wasted time and estimated 643 KiB image-delivery savings; the HAR transferred 1,026,355 bytes over 45 requests.
Lighthouse estimated 89 KiB of unused JavaScript: about 70 KiB from Google Tag Manager and 21 KiB from jQuery 3.4.1.
The detail probe found Server controls as clickable list items and rating actions as SPAN elements with tabindex=-1; they are not exposed as operable buttons.
Lighthouse measured 3.45:1 for white text on the active #ff4141 navigation chip, 3.84:1 for pagination text, and 3.59:1 for the footer link, below 4.5:1.
A direct focus probe confirmed document.activeElement was the search input while its computed outline was none and box-shadow was none.
Mobile and desktop captures show readable line spacing and stable two-column reflow; card truncation uses ellipsis without clipping the grid.
The probe measured the search submit at 32×28 px and many navigation/text links at 40 px or 32 px tall. The viewport itself permits zoom and reflows without horizontal overflow.
Lighthouse’s errors-in-console audit scored 1 with zero logged browser errors.
Lighthouse reported displayed ratios around 1.45 versus source ratios around 1.43, while markup declares 320×180 for 500×350 files; the image audit also found 28 oversized images.
Lighthouse reported three deprecations from the Cloudflare challenge script, including Shared Storage and Protected Audience API warnings.
The probe found a descriptive title and meta description; detail pages also use a content-specific title.
Lighthouse passed crawlable anchors, link text, robots, and viewport audits; raw content coverage was 100%.
The fetched robots.txt contains “Sitemap: https:/sexmupxinh.net/sitemap.xml” with only one slash after the scheme, even though /sitemap.xml itself returns 200.
The detail probe found only BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. The page represents a video and exposes title/description/player information, but no VideoObject entity is provided.
The header audit found no CSP or HSTS. Cookie evidence found both _ga cookies lacked Secure, used SameSite=None, and persisted for 400 days.
The tracker audit found 8 third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics. The HAR records third-party scripts and the 12-second screenshot shows no privacy choice.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No authentication surface or permission request exists on the audited public video/listing flows.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site exposes neither authentication nor permission-gated capability on audited paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Headers evidence found no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or CSP; only X-Content-Type-Options was present.
Discoverability evidence measured 100% raw/rendered content coverage, no JS shell, and matching title/H1/description without JavaScript.
Across desktop and mobile detail captures, the player iframe rendered a browser failure icon while the surrounding page stayed live; no fallback player or semantic error state replaced it.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: This is a public streaming/content MPA rather than an installable app, and playback intrinsically requires network media.
checkOutcomes.reason: Installability/offline playback is not proportionate for this network-dependent content site.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The broken media surface provides neither a timeout message nor retry. By contrast, the tested 404 and empty-search pages do provide clear messages, isolating the gap to playback.
The document correctly declares lang=vi, but the platform probe found no logical CSS properties; the captured stylesheet repeatedly uses left, right, margin-left, and padding-left.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Audited templates present no dates, numbers, prices, currencies, durations, or calendar values requiring locale formatting.
checkOutcomes.reason: No locale-sensitive data appears on the audited templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No scheduled events or time-zone-sensitive values appear on audited paths.
No consent wall, confirmshaming, forced continuity, disguised control, or subscription upsell appeared on initial or delayed loads; navigation and outbound actions are visually distinct.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The only form is an optional search field with no invalid/required state. Empty search results are explained clearly.
checkOutcomes.reason: No form with user-validation requirements exists; empty search is a result state, not invalid input.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The only input is a free-text site search, for which address/payment/sign-in autocomplete tokens do not apply; it accepts text without obstruction.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No checkout, subscription, consent, authentication, or account-management flow is exposed on audited paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No commercial or account flow exists in scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The image audit found 28 oversized images, 29 images without srcset, 29 legacy-format images, and zero modern-format images. Lighthouse estimated 643 KiB potential image savings.
Trace/layout evidence recorded no long tasks, content is server-rendered, and below-fold thumbnails use lazy loading.
The page contacts 8 third-party origins; Lighthouse attributes about 70 KiB unused JavaScript to GTM and about 21 KiB to jQuery, while the page’s core listing can render server-side without them.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No declared intent indicates agent-facing transactions or tools; this public content catalogue has no action requiring WebMCP exposure.
checkOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing capability or developer intent was identified.

checkOutcomes.method: Applicability judgement from recon and representative-path DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The experience has no summarization or inference task where on-device AI is necessary.
checkOutcomes.reason: No appropriate on-device inference use case was identified.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten real server-control toggles, heap size was 6.49 MB versus 6.24 MB baseline (+4.0%) and node count 137,360 versus 134,929 (+1.8%); this bounded one-pass growth does not indicate an unbounded leak.
The detail page baseline heap was 6.24 MB across 134,929 nodes, proportionate to a page with an embedded player and scripts.
Baseline/post heap top constructors contained no Detached* population, and the small node increase after ten toggles did not show a growing detached-DOM signature.

principleOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing capability or developer intent was identified. No appropriate on-device inference use case was identified.

paths.description: Homepage/new-video listing: primary discovery template and global chrome.
Japanese category: representative category/listing archetype; other category pages share this template.
Search results plus a no-results query: representative input and empty-state flow.
Video detail/player: primary consumption flow and the highest-risk interactive template.
Unknown route: representative HTTP/network recovery template and indexing behavior.

findings.summary: The site is hard-coded to one dark palette instead of following the user’s light/dark preference.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule, and default and dark-emulated screenshots are byte-identical (229,260 bytes).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Route changes and state changes swap abruptly without View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS/DOM inspection found no view-transition-name, @view-transition, or startViewTransition usage across the listing and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for MPA navigation, with directional cues where they clarify forward/back movement.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on the search input, and several mobile controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focused search field computed to outline: none and no box-shadow. The submit control measured 32×28 px and the text input 170×28 px, below the 44×44 CSS-pixel target guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px without shrinking visible layout unnecessarily.

findings.summary: The representative watch flow reaches a broken player instead of playable media.
findings.evidence: After 5 seconds on the detail page at desktop and mobile sizes, the 16:9 player showed a broken-document icon. The iframe URL was present, but the core playback surface did not render.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a reliable player endpoint, detect embed/load failure, and offer a first-party fallback or alternate server that users can activate accessibly.

findings.summary: The failed player state has no explanation or recovery action.
findings.evidence: The detail screenshot shows only the browser broken-resource icon; there is no status text, retry action, or accessible error announcement near the player.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the opaque iframe failure with a monitored loading/error state that explains the problem and offers Retry and alternate-server actions.

findings.summary: Mobile lab LCP exceeds the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.0 s (score 0.77), above the 2.5 s good threshold, although the local trace measured 1.11 s and TBT remained low.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP resource, reduce its bytes, and remove avoidable render-blocking work; verify with repeat mobile Lighthouse and field data.

findings.summary: Render-blocking CSS and inefficient image delivery delay useful content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified a Google font stylesheet with about 812 ms wasted time and estimated 643 KiB image-delivery savings; the HAR transferred 1,026,355 bytes over 45 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused icon-font CSS, inline or preload only critical CSS, and serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP images through srcset/sizes.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 89 KiB of unused JavaScript: about 70 KiB from Google Tag Manager and 21 KiB from jQuery 3.4.1.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove jQuery if native APIs cover its uses, and load analytics only after consent/need with a smaller, deferred integration.

findings.summary: Player controls are implemented as non-semantic, non-keyboard controls.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found Server controls as clickable list items and rating actions as SPAN elements with tabindex=-1; they are not exposed as operable buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native button elements for server, like, and dislike actions, preserving accessible names, pressed state, and keyboard activation.

findings.summary: Several text/control combinations fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.45:1 for white text on the active #ff4141 navigation chip, 3.84:1 for pagination text, and 3.59:1 for the footer link, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to reach at least 4.5:1 for normal text and retest all interactive states.

findings.summary: Keyboard users cannot see focus on the search field.
findings.evidence: A direct focus probe confirmed document.activeElement was the search input while its computed outline was none and box-shadow was none.
findings.suggestedFix: Define an obvious, high-contrast :focus-visible ring for all interactive elements; do not suppress the browser outline without a replacement.

findings.summary: Touch targets are too small on the mobile template.
findings.evidence: The probe measured the search submit at 32×28 px and many navigation/text links at 40 px or 32 px tall. The viewport itself permits zoom and reflows without horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px while keeping the fluid two-column layout and user-scalable viewport.

findings.summary: Thumbnail dimensions/aspect ratios do not match the delivered images.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported displayed ratios around 1.45 versus source ratios around 1.43, while markup declares 320×180 for 500×350 files; the image audit also found 28 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate thumbnails at the intended aspect ratio and declare matching intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio values.

findings.summary: A Cloudflare script triggers deprecated API warnings.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecations from the Cloudflare challenge script, including Shared Storage and Protected Audience API warnings.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or reconfigure the Cloudflare challenge integration and confirm current scripts no longer invoke deprecated browser APIs.

findings.summary: robots.txt declares a malformed Sitemap URL.
findings.evidence: The fetched robots.txt contains “Sitemap: https:/sexmupxinh.net/sitemap.xml” with only one slash after the scheme, even though /sitemap.xml itself returns 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the directive to https://sexmupxinh.net/sitemap.xml and validate robots/sitemap consistency after deployment.

findings.summary: Video detail pages omit VideoObject structured data.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found only BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. The page represents a video and exposes title/description/player information, but no VideoObject entity is provided.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD, including name, description, thumbnailUrl, uploadDate when known, and embedUrl/contentUrl that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Important transport defenses are missing and analytics cookies are insecure.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no CSP or HSTS. Cookie evidence found both _ga cookies lacked Secure, used SameSite=None, and persisted for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and a tested CSP, and set analytics cookies Secure with an appropriate SameSite policy and shorter retention.

findings.summary: The page loads a broad tracking/third-party footprint without an evident consent choice.
findings.evidence: The tracker audit found 8 third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics. The HAR records third-party scripts and the 12-second screenshot shows no privacy choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize third parties, gate non-essential analytics on informed consent, shorten retention, and document each remaining processor and purpose.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policies are largely absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or CSP; only X-Content-Type-Options was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options where needed), strict Referrer-Policy, least-privilege Permissions-Policy, HSTS, and a nonce/hash-based CSP.

findings.summary: The embedded player does not degrade robustly when its external runtime fails.
findings.evidence: Across desktop and mobile detail captures, the player iframe rendered a browser failure icon while the surrounding page stayed live; no fallback player or semantic error state replaced it.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat the embed as an enhancement: monitor it, time out cleanly, and replace it with an accessible fallback plus alternate-server controls implemented as buttons.

findings.summary: Media/network failure is not translated into a useful recovery state.
findings.evidence: The broken media surface provides neither a timeout message nor retry. By contrast, the tested 404 and empty-search pages do provide clear messages, isolating the gap to playback.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle iframe/media load errors and timeouts with explicit status, Retry, and alternate-source options while preserving page context.

findings.summary: The stylesheet is tied to physical left/right directions.
findings.evidence: The document correctly declares lang=vi, but the platform probe found no logical CSS properties; the captured stylesheet repeatedly uses left, right, margin-left, and padding-left.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep lang=vi and migrate layout-affecting rules to margin-inline, padding-inline, inset-inline, and inline-size so bidi/localized layouts remain viable.

findings.summary: Almost every thumbnail is oversized, legacy-format, and non-responsive.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 28 oversized images, 29 images without srcset, 29 legacy-format images, and zero modern-format images. Lighthouse estimated 643 KiB potential image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Create AVIF/WebP variants at several widths, emit srcset/sizes, preserve matching intrinsic dimensions, and keep below-fold lazy loading.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume bytes without proportionate visible value.
findings.evidence: The page contacts 8 third-party origins; Lighthouse attributes about 70 KiB unused JavaScript to GTM and about 21 KiB to jQuery, while the page’s core listing can render server-side without them.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary third parties, replace jQuery with native code, and defer consented analytics until after core content is interactive.

taskList.title: Make player failure observable and recoverable, with a reliable fallback
Deploy CSP/HSTS/clickjacking/privacy policies and secure analytics cookies
Generate responsive AVIF/WebP thumbnails with matching intrinsic dimensions
Restore visible keyboard focus, semantic media controls, contrast, and 44px targets
Remove unused jQuery/analytics cost and defer consented third parties
Add VideoObject metadata and fix the robots.txt Sitemap URL
Add preference-driven theming and progressive route transitions
Adopt logical CSS properties and clear remaining platform warnings
